@@ -78,6 +78,7 @@ The server exposes tools across three modules in `crates/app/src/mcp/` (see `cra
 - `set_wcs { "origin"?: [x, y, z], "stock_point"?: string, "offset"?: [dx, dy, dz], "rotation"?: [qx, qy, qz, qw] }`: Place the active setup's WCS origin and orientation quaternion.
 - `set_wcs_circle_centre { "edge": { "model": string, "id": "chain:0x…" }, "rotation"?: [qx, qy, qz, qw] }`: Place the active setup's WCS origin on the centre of a picked circular edge (a hole rim or boss edge, full circle or arc), at the edge's height; returns the circle's centre, axis and diameter. Refuses a straight edge, a non-circular curve, a face or a vertex by name (#739).
 - `set_wcs_from_features { "picks": [{ "model": string, "id": string, "role": "origin" | "x" | "y" | "z" }], "setup"?: string }`: Place the active setup's WCS on a frame fitted to `list_features` picks - the GUI's "Set WCS from features" law (#701, #937). Axes read in Z, X, Y priority: the first axis pick is exact, the second squared to it, the third derived right-handed. A flat face sets its outward normal, a straight edge its direction, a curved wall (face or patch) its fitted axis; the origin is a vertex, a face's centroid or a wall's centre (else the second axis pick's anchor), projected onto the first pick's plane when that is a face. One undo step. Refused by name: under two picks, a role given twice, under two axes, a pick that cannot set its role, near-parallel axes (< 5 deg), a stale id, a `setup` that is not the active one. Note: a `list_features` face row's `normal` and `facing` are the outward side (#956). Where the outside cannot be told (an open or inside-out shell) both are null and `outside_unknown` holds the reason (#2186); tell such faces apart by `bounds`, or repair the mesh.
+- `set_wcs_flip { "x"?: bool, "y"?: bool, "z"?: bool, "setup"?: string }`: Set which axes of a setup's WCS run reversed (a flip: X+ becomes X-), as the WCS page's Flip X / Flip Y / Flip Z buttons do (#1720). An axis not given keeps its flag; the origin and rotation do not change. One undo step. Returns `{ setup, label, flip: {x, y, z}, refused }`. Posting or generating with a flipped WCS is not available yet: the post and every generation in that setup are refused by name (`refused` holds the text) until the flip is cleared. `get_job`'s `setups[].wcs.flip` shows the flags. Refused by name: no flag given, a flag that is not a boolean, an unknown setup.
 - `set_work_offset { "index": integer | "G54".."G59" | null, "word"?: (alias of index), "setup"?: string }`: Set the work offset a declared setup posts at (#931). `index` is 1-based, up to the maximum of the setup's own post (6 on most posts, 9 on Tormach PathPilot); the words `G54`–`G59` are accepted as aliases of 1–6, and `word` is the older spelling of the same argument (give one, or both agreeing). An offset the setup's post cannot express is refused by setup name (e.g. `setup Setup1 uses work offset 7, but its post ... expresses work offsets 1-6 only`). `null` clears it (offset 1). Returns `{ setup, index, name, word, label }`: `name` is what the post calls the offset (e.g. `G55`, `G59.1`, or `work offset 9` when the post gives none); `word` is kept as an alias of `name`. `get_job`'s `setups[].wcs` and `set_wcs` carry the same `index` / `name` / `word`.
 - `load_machine { "builtin"?: string, "path"?: string, "clear"?: boolean, "setup"?: string }`: Mount a machine configuration at document or setup level: a built-in preset by name (`"VMC 3-axis"`, `"Lathe"`, the Tormach models, ...) or a `.mch` file by path; `clear: true` mounts none.
 - `set_workholding_max_rpm { "max_rpm": number | null, "setup"?: string }`: State the rated maximum rpm of a setup's chuck or collet; `null` clears it. Refused with a named error: a missing or non-numeric value, zero, negative or non-finite numbers, anything under 1 rpm or over 100000 rpm, an unknown setup, and a value the setup already states. `setup` defaults to the active one. One undo step. At post time, a constant-rpm (G97) turning operation faster than the limit is refused by name, and a constant-surface-speed (G96) section's rpm ceiling is capped at it (Fanuc `G50 S`, Tormach `G96 D`).

+## #1720 - WCS axis flip: stored flags, refused at post and generation
+
+**Decided (taken unattended, issue-worker-high):**
+
+1. **Where the flags live.** A new component `schema::WcsFlip([bool; 3])`
+   on the setup's WCS entity, next to its `Location`. Not on `SetupDef`:
+   the flip belongs to the frame, and every place that moves, deletes or
+   copies the WCS entity (DeleteEntity, DeleteSetup, CreateSetup's datum
+   transfer) now carries it with the location. "No flip" is stored as no
+   component, so a world without flips is unchanged.
+2. **Project file.** An optional `flip` object on the entity row, with
+   keys `x`, `y`, `z`; only a flipped axis is written (`{"x": true}`), and
+   a row with no flip writes no key. A file without the key opens with no
+   flip. A `flip` on a row that is not a WCS is refused as corrupt by
+   name. `PROJECT_VERSION` goes from 66 to 67, because an older reader
+   would silently drop the flip and post a program that does not match
+   the stored frame once part 2 lands.
+3. **Refusal, not output.** Part 1 changes no posted G-code. A flipped
+   WCS is refused by name at the one generation door (`collect_job`, next
+   to the #1510 tilt check) and in the post's verification gate (next to
+   #315's rotated-offset clause), so every post path refuses it. The post
+   clause gives one line per flipped setup, in first-use program order,
+   with the operations that use it; suppressed operations are skipped,
+   as the rotated-offset clause does.
+4. **The command places a WCS when none exists.** `SetWcsFlip` on a setup
+   whose WCS was never placed spawns it at the identity (what
+   `SetWcsOrigin` would do), and its undo removes it again. Considered:
+   refusing the flip until the origin is set; dropped, because the page
+   shows the buttons on an unplaced WCS and a refusal there reads as a
+   broken button.
+5. **The datum transfer copies the flip.** When `CreateSetup` clones an
+   existing setup's WCS into the new setup, the flip is cloned with the
+   location (the new frame is the same frame until the user changes it);
+   undo removes the clone. Materializing `Setup1` from a document with no
+   setups keeps the WCS entity it points at, flip included. Considered:
+   a clone that starts unflipped; dropped, because a copied frame that
+   silently loses an axis direction is not the same frame.
+6. **The gizmo shows the flip.** A flipped axis is drawn reversed, and a
+   flipped WCS at the origin does not hide the world axes (it is not the
+   world frame).
+7. **No script verb.** The MCP tool `set_wcs_flip` covers the agent
+   surface; the script language has no WCS verb family to join yet.
+
+**Considered and dropped:** a signed scale per axis (`[f64; 3]` of +-1):
+it admits values that mean nothing; three booleans do not.
+
+**Cost to change later:** the key shape is in v67 files; renaming it needs
+a migration step. Part 2 (posting with a flip) replaces the two refusals
+with the frame work and keeps the stored flags.
